message.content:
Yes—if you’re experiencing excessive or disruptive noise in Atlanta, you can file a complaint with the city’s authorities. In most cases, the City of Atlanta Police Department (or the City’s Office of Noise Control) will handle noise complaints. Here’s how you can do it:

| Step | What to Do | Where to Go / Who to Contact |
|------|------------|------------------------------|
| **1** | **Identify the source and time** – Note the address, the type of noise (e.g., construction, loud music, barking dogs), and when it occurs. | N/A |
| **2** | **Call 311** – Atlanta’s non-emergency hotline (311) will connect you to the appropriate department. | 311 (within Atlanta) |
| **3** | **Use the online portal** – You can submit a noise complaint online via the City of Atlanta’s official website. | https://www.atlantaga.gov/311 |
| **4** | **Contact the Police Department** – If the noise is urgent or you suspect illegal activity, you can call the Atlanta Police Department’s non-emergency line. | 404‑555‑1234 (non‑emergency) |
| **5** | **Follow up** – After filing, you’ll receive a reference number. Keep it handy for any follow‑up questions or to check the status of your complaint. | N/A |

### Quick Tips

- **Provide details**: The more information you give (exact location, time, description), the easier it is for officials to investigate.
- **Check local ordinances**: Atlanta has specific noise ordinances that define permissible decibel levels and quiet hours (typically 10 p.m.–7 a.m.). Knowing these can help you frame your complaint.
- **Document evidence**: If possible, record audio or take photos that illustrate the disturbance. This can support your claim.

If you’re unsure whether a particular situation falls under a noise ordinance, you can also ask the 311 operator for clarification before filing.
